<coding_guidelines>
# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: the walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`, `observatory-cli replay` over
one captured session, an empty board that starts) is integrated on `mission/observatory-v1`
(2026-10-23). Each later milestone deepens one area from it.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: N`: `2027` on the S fixture
   (`2026-10-22-observatory-v1-s.jsonl`, the mapper knows no kind yet), `0` from the M0 fixture
   onward.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to `BACKLOG.md` as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs or GitHub issues
  (rule 14; owner decision 2026-10-22 at mission approval).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

1→# User testing
2→
3→**What belongs here:** the surfaces a validator can drive, the exact commands that worked on this machine
4→(validation readiness report, 2026-10-22), the oracle commands, the evidence to collect, the cost class of
5→each surface and how validators isolate from each other. Sections marked "to be filled by validators"
6→collect runtime findings as milestones land.
7→
8→**What does not belong here:** start/stop/healthcheck commands and ports (`services.yaml`), machine facts
9→(`environment.md`), Rust test conventions (`rust-conventions.md`).
10→
11→## Surfaces at a glance
12→
13→| Surface | What it proves | Driver | Cost class |
14→|---|---|---|---|
15→| CLI (`observatory-cli replay`, `inspect`, `metrics --csv`) and `cargo test` | mapping, counts, pointers, metrics; the oracle for everything else | shell | low (warm `cargo test` 2.6 s in the scratch crate) |
16→| Browser host: `trunk serve` on 3141 | the board and every view-model in a real browser (primary interactive surface, SPEC §6) | `agent-browser` | medium: trunk 35 MB idle, each browser session 1.34-1.54 GB RSS, max 3 sessions |
17→| Tauri window: `make app-dev` | the native shell starts, loads the same UI, wires commands (smoke check, planning note 4) | `ps`, log, `lsof`, `osascript`, `screencapture` | high during the build (37.66 s to the app process, native rustc burst), low idle (130 MB RSS) |
18→| Live attach / host | a real `droid exec --mission` appears on the board within 1 s (M1), hosted mission controls (M2) | terminal + board | medium (a Droid session plus the board) |
19→| `cargo llvm-cov` | coverage floor | shell | high: load 3.3 to 14.6 on 10 cores; runs alone |
20→| GitHub via `gh api` | PR, runs, statuses, rulesets for the gate lane (M4) | `gh` | low |
21→
22→Serialize anything that compiles: cargo builds share the `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `cargo llvm-cov` and the
23→first `cargo tauri dev` build run with nothing else compiling. Validators run user tests only after builds
24→finish.
25→
26→## Browser host (primary)
27→
28→Start `trunk-ui` from `services.yaml` and wait for `curl -sf http://localhost:3141/` (55.94 s cold, then
29→1.46-2.08 s per incremental rebuild). Then, exactly as they worked on 2026-10-22:
30→
31→```sh
32→until curl -sf -o /dev/null http://localhost:3141/; do sleep 1; done
33→agent-browser open http://localhost:3141          # 1.25 s
34→agent-browser snapshot                            # accessibility tree with refs: heading ... [ref=e1], button ... [ref=e2]
35→agent-browser snapshot -i                         # interactive elements only
36→agent-browser click @e2                           # click by ref
37→agent-browser get title
38→agent-browser get text body
39→agent-browser screenshot /tmp/observatory-<milestone>-<scenario>.png
40→agent-browser console                             # expect empty
41→agent-browser errors                              # expect empty
42→agent-browser --session <name> open http://localhost:3141   # isolated second validator (own Chrome, own page state)
43→agent-browser session list
44→agent-browser close --all                         # at the end; daemons otherwise linger 1 h
45→```
46→
47→Rules:
48→
49→- One `--session <name>` per validator (`default` is a session too); at most 3 sessions per `trunk serve`;
50→  never more than 5. Sessions are isolated (verified: `clicks: 1` in `default` while `val2` showed `clicks: 0`).
51→- Read the page through `snapshot`, not the raw HTML: the dev page carries trunk's live-reload script
52→  (websocket `/.well-known/trunk/ws`) at the top of `<body>`; the app is inside `<main>`.
53→- Evidence per scenario: the snapshot lines you asserted on (with refs), the screenshot path and byte size
54→  (`Screenshot saved to ... (12217 bytes)` style), `console` and `errors` output, and the CLI oracle output
55→  for the same fixture.
56→- `agent-browser` cannot attach to the Tauri window (no CDP endpoint; `connect 9229` fails with
57→  `All CDP discovery methods failed`). A failed `connect` leaves a daemon entry; close it.
58→
59→### Opening a fixture in the browser host
60→
61→The UI's `BrowserBackend` (architecture §7) reads the fixture through an `<input type=file>` file picker,
62→runs `mapping::map_record` and `core::view` in wasm, with no store. The exact agent-browser steps (which ref
63→the input has, which command sets a file on it, whether a `.capture.json` or the root `.jsonl` is picked,
64→how the children directory is supplied) are not known until the UI exists.
65→
66→**To be filled by the M1 ui-worker:** the exact commands, the expected `MissionSummary` text on screen
67→(`event_count`, `unknown_count`, `mapping_version`) and the fixture used
68→(`fixtures/streams/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.jsonl`).

70→## Tauri window (smoke check)
71→
72→Owner decision (planning note 4): the Tauri window is validated as a smoke check; the functional evidence is
73→the browser host. Procedure, with the commands that worked:
74→
75→1. Make sure no other trunk owns 3141 (`lsof -nP -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:LISTEN`, exit 1 = free), then start
76→   `tauri-dev` from `services.yaml` (log `/tmp/observatory-tauri.log`). Start it (and any `trunk serve`)
77→   with Execute `fireAndForget: true`; a `nohup ... &` in a normal call dies when the call returns
78→   (observed by the s-app-empty-lanes worker). `make app-dev` passed this smoke set on 2026-10-22
79→   (cargo-tauri, trunk, observatory-app PIDs; WebKit ESTABLISHED to [::1]:3141).
80→2. Wait for the line `Running /home/user/.cargo/shared_rust_target/debug/observatory-app` in the log
81→   (37.66 s after launch with warm wasm; 31.18 s of it is the native build) and check that no panic follows.
82→3. Process alive:
83→
84→   ```sh
85→   ps -axo pid,command | awk '$2 ~ /shared_rust_target\/debug\/observatory-app$/ {print $1}'
86→   ps -p <pid> -o pid,rss,%cpu,command          # 130 MB RSS, 0.0 %CPU idle in the readiness run
87→   ```
88→
89→4. The webview fetched the page: `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141` shows `com.apple.WebKit` (or `com.apple ...`)
90→   `ESTABLISHED` connections to `[::1]:3141` (three in the readiness run).
91→5. System Events lists the app as a foreground process:
92→
93→   ```sh
94→   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get name of every process whose background only is false'
95→   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to get {name, unix id, frontmost, visible} of process "observatory-app"'
96→   osascript -e 'tell application "System Events" to tell process "observatory-app" to count windows'   # 1 when the display is unlocked
97→   ```
98→
99→6. Screenshot only when the display is unlocked: check
100→   `ioreg -n Root -d1 -a | grep -A1 CGSSessionScreenIsLocked` first; locked gives a uniformly black frame
101→   (`YAVG=16`) and `count windows` 0. Then `screencapture -x /tmp/observatory-tauri-<milestone>.png` and verify
102→   with `ffmpeg -hide_banner -i <png> -vf signalstats,metadata=print:key=lavfi.signalstats.YAVG:file=- -f null - 2>/dev/null | grep YAVG`.
103→   If the display is locked, record process/log/System-Events evidence and say so; the owner's screenshot
104→   (below) is the human-captured frame.
105→7. Shutdown: kill cargo-tauri, `trunk serve` and the app binary by PID (killing cargo-tauri alone orphans the
106→   other two, trunk keeps 3141 bound). `services.yaml` `tauri-dev.stop` does this. Confirm with
107→   `lsof -nP -iTCP:3141 -sTCP:LISTEN` (exit 1) and the System Events list.
108→
109→Whether a window-level screenshot works on an unlocked screen is unverified (the readiness run had the
110→screen locked). **To be filled by validators:** the first unlocked `count windows` and `screencapture` result,
111→with the window title (`app.windows[].title`, `droid-observatory`).

113→## CLI oracle
114→
115→All from the worktree (`services.yaml` `replay`, `inspect`, `metrics-csv`):
116→
117→```sh
118→cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl        # prints lane events, ends with `unknown events: N`; exit 0
119→cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- replay /nonexistent.jsonl; echo $?           # non-zero (cli_exits_nonzero_on_missing_file)
120→cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- inspect <event-id>                             # the exact raw bytes of the line by pointer; `--scrub` applies the B-006 pass
121→cargo run -q -p observatory-cli -- metrics fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl --csv # M5; compared to reports/reference/2026-10-22-observatory-v1-m0.csv within 1 s, 1 token, 0.01 USD

123→```

127→on the M0 capture; S allows N > 0.

129→## Store
130→
131→`[store].path` defaults to `~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite`; a validator overrides it through a temp
132→config (`OBSERVATORY_CONFIG=<path>`, see Isolation). Inspect read-only:

134→```sh
135→sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite '.tables'
136→sqlite3 -readonly ~/.droid-observatory/observatory.sqlite 'select count(*) from events;'

161→## Live attach and host
162→
163→- Attach (M1): with the board open, start a `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal on a scratch directory
164→  inside the worktree (`target/scratch/<name>`); the new session must appear on the board and each event
165→  within 1 s. Latency evidence: the `attach_latency.rs` harness output (`p50/p95/max`, pasted) plus validator

168→  reach the orchestrator; hosted and attached views agree on the event count; the child process is reaped on

172→## Resource cost and scheduling
173→
174→| Class | Surfaces | Rule |
175→|---|---|---|
176→| low | CLI oracle, `cargo test` (warm), `gh api`, `sqlite3`, agent-browser idle | run freely; cargo waits on the shared lock if a build is in flight |
177→| medium | `trunk serve` with up to 3 agent-browser sessions (1.5 GB each upper bound), a live Droid session | one trunk on 3141; close sessions when done |

192→  under `/home/user/.factory/sessions/` or another worktree.

194→- Keychain values are never printed; `security find-generic-password -s <service>` without `-w` is the only
